verdicts.note: Supports the council-imposed 0.1% public-safety sales tax as 'a stable, dedicated funding source' in two separate interviews [S9][S14]. Explicit support for new revenue, but a flat sales tax rather than progressive revenue, so +1 medium.

Her stated tools are growth management (smaller rural growth area, urban and infrastructure-served housing, cottage housing) [S6][S9], not deregulation or public housing and tenant protections; the statement's 'creating affordable housing while protecting our natural environment' [S15] names no mechanism. 0 at low is honest.

Pole A: more sheriff staffing, 'a stronger law enforcement presence', the sales tax for recruitment and retention, and a Gig Harbor vote to increase police staffing [S6][S9][S11]; her statement lists 'investing in public safety' first [S15]. Pole B: mental-health responders, violence prevention and the sheriff-ombuds amendment [S6][S14]. Balanced, 0 medium.

Calls environmental protection an investment in 'climate resilience' and lists shoreline, forest and habitat protection [S6][S9]; her statement says she supported environmental protections on the Gig Harbor council [S15]. Medium rests on her statements, not the Washington Conservation Action endorsement.
Former Gig Harbor councilmember and mayor pro tem, Regional Council representative, current Charter Review commissioner, running for an open seat [S5][S11][S15]. Short tenure keeps it at -1.

Opposes the 0.1% sales tax as passed 'without a vote of the people' but says he would have backed a version limited to law enforcement and corrections [S5]; his statement adds 'double-layered taxes' and 'rising county costs' [S11]. The conditional support keeps it at -1 medium.

Repeated across four sources in his own words: the county 'spends too much money and has not budgeted within its means', fund mandates and basic services first [S5]; 'measurable outcomes ... regular review of county programs' [S2]; an 'emergency audit' of the budget [S10]; 'laser focused' on 'fiscal accountability' [S11]. That is pole A almost word for word, and the repetition meets the guide's 'high'. His wish for a better deputies' contract and a Fox Island bridge plan are priorities inside the budget, which he proposes to fund partly by selling county land [S5], not a pro-expansion stance. -2 high holds.

Says regulation 'stifles growth' and would 'cut the red tape' for 'a predictable land use process' [S5], with 'reasonable growth standards' in his statement [S11]. Pole A in his own words; the parks-conservation line keeps it at -1 medium.

Deputy recruitment, staffing and retention at the center of the platform [S2][S5], 'public safety, deputy staffing' in his statement [S11], and opposition to the sheriff-ombuds as 'activist led' [S10]. The basis rests on those stated positions, not the guild or police-union endorsements [S4]. Nothing on prosecution, encampments or treatment, which is why medium.
First run for office, 'not a career politician' [S5][S11]; 27 years in policing and six as guild president [S7][S11] is an institutional background, so +1 rather than +2.

missing.basis: Her statement says she will 'prioritize investing in public safety, expanding broadband access' and expand 'job training and workforce development programs' [S15]. She backs the new 0.1% sales tax to fund deputy 'recruitment, retention, and training' and says District 7 needs more Peninsula Detachment staffing [S9]. That is the invest-and-expand pole. Her one restraint line, spending taxpayer dollars 'responsibly and effectively' [S6], is boilerplate. Solan is at -2 on this axis, so it is the race's clearest fiscal contrast.
